:::

## What you should be able to do tonight

- Derive the price at which a leveraged long position gets a maintenance margin call, from equity, position value and the maintenance fraction.
- Say what forced deleveraging does to a crowded position, and why it makes correlations rise exactly when you do not want them to.

## Tasks <span class='task-total'>60 min</span>

::: {.task-list}
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [25 min]{.task-min} Derive it rather than look it up: with initial equity E, borrowing to hold N shares at price P, and maintenance requirement m, find the price at which equity divided by position value falls to m. Then evaluate it for 2 to 1 leverage at m equal to 0.25.
:::
::: {.task}

Note where a 33 percent drawdown in the index becomes something else entirely.
:::
